back: A theory of what motivates people, by identifying their needs: Maslow, Herzberg and McClelland.
A theory of how people decide to make an effort, by looking at the thinking linking effort, performance and reward: Vroom.
Achievement (challenge, feedback), power (influence, lead), affiliation (belonging, friendly relationships). One tends to dominate.
Achievement: target-driven jobs; power: management and leadership; affiliation: teamwork and customer service.
The belief that effort will lead to good performance. Raised by training, resources and achievable targets.
The belief that good performance will lead to a reward. Raised by clear rules and keeping promises.
How much the person values the reward. Raised by finding out what employees want.
McClelland: needs hard to measure and may change. Vroom: assumes rational calculation; hard to measure each belief for each person.

front: All three beliefs must be present
back: If expectancy, instrumentality or valence is close to zero, motivation to make an effort is low.
